Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Safety-tier review. No blocking findings.

What looks good:

- The option is off by default. Each new G84 group has M29 S600 on the block directly before it in the test program. The drill has no M29.
- A tap with no spindle speed gives a named warning and writes no M29 or G84.
- The change is a part of #2603. `Refs #2603` keeps that issue open for its other questions.

Local results with main:

- PR head: `0fa08c5922b24a638806b96fc872783a94e6579f`.
- Main: `f14097855b0e347a073f1e8cc74a889554e6dbbb`.
- Trial merge: `39814f33347997b572c41c2d52c3ff5ca2541997`. Its first parent is the PR head. The merge has no conflicts.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. 121 steps; 119 test suites; 842 tests passed; one ignored; no failures.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: PASS. 27 steps; 26 selected suites. One ignored test ran and passed: `every_slow_kind_on_a_mill_turn_keeps_the_work_spindle_within_the_chuck`. The other selected suites had no ignored tests.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- The build gives an existing workspace warning for the unused `truck-polymesh` dependency. Clippy has no errors.
- All commands ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3468`. No GitHub runner or workflow was used.

Extra suites run:

- No extra importer or fixture suites apply. The PR changes no importer, fixture, testdata file, or golden file.
- The full `fanuc_rigid_tap` suite ran in quick: all four tests passed. `fanuc_aicc`, `rigid_tapping`, `conformance`, and `posting` also passed.

Mutations:

1. Remove the M29 output from a copy of the post in `/tmp`: RED. The check for M29 directly before all three G84 groups fails. Use the unchanged post: GREEN.
2. Remove the spindle-speed guard from a copy of the post in `/tmp`: RED. The check for the named refusal and no M29/G84 fails. Use the unchanged post: GREEN.

These checks used the post CLI with the PR's STREAM and NO_RPM inputs and the same output checks as its tests. No repository source was changed. A local check script first assumed that the CLI always creates a warning file. It was corrected to accept no file when there are no warnings; all mutation checks then completed.

Goldens and output:

- No golden files moved. I read all new G-code output from the three tap groups and the drill group. Each G80 ends a group; the next G84 has its own M29, with no intervening axis move.
- With the option off, the test program and warning output have the same bytes as upstream main.
- This review does not include a check on a machine control.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes:

- The review supplies the mapped heavy-gate result absent from the PR body. The feature follows the normal minor-cut merge rule.
- The warm worktree and branch remain in place. No code, images, logs, or review evidence were committed or pushed.

Second read after the merge (read-only, not built) of head 0fa08c5922b24a638806b96fc872783a94e6579f.

Verdict: no defect found by reading. The merge is `ce9d0d521`.

Checks (line numbers are `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` on `origin/main`):

1. Option off. The default is `false` (line 64). The test `fanuc_rigid_tap_m29_option_is_declared_off` pins it. The two new statements (lines 1179-1182 and 1197) run only when `optBool("rigidTapM29", false)` is true. No other line of the post changed. Thus the output with the option off is byte-identical by reading. No golden moved in the diff.
2. Option on. The blocks of a new group are `G80` (if a group is open), `G99`, `M29 S<rpm>`, `G84 X Y Z R F` (lines 1193-1206). No axis move is between `M29` and `G84`.
   - The S value is `sRpm`, the same value that the section start writes in `S<rpm> M3` (line 756).
   - The post writes no `G94` or `G95`. Thus F is feed per minute. The post does not check that F / S is the pitch. The stream supplies F. In the test, F600 and S600 give 1.0 mm, the pitch of an M6 tap.
   - `M29` is written for each new G84 group. A group ends at `G80`, and the hop law of #994 gives one group for each hole in the test (3 groups, 3 `M29`).
   - A tool change starts a new section. The section writes `G80` (line 744), so the next G84 opens a new group with a new `M29 S`.
   - A G84 dwell is refused by name (#2356, line 1174). A Q word is not written for TAP (line 1200). This is not new.
   - A left-hand tap is refused before the post, in `crates/app/src/posting_family.rs:42`. No `G74` is written.
3. With the option on, a section with no speed or 0 rpm gives the named refusal (line 1179) and writes no `M29` and no `G84`. A section that is not a probe section is refused before that, by `spindleStopped` (line 1178). A pitch of 0 gives F = 0. The refusal of #1357 (line 1154) stops that cycle. No `M29 S0` is possible.
4. Scope. Only `fanuc.cps` changed. `doosan-dnm.cps` and `dialect.rs` name `fanuc.cps` only in a comment and a test. The two new statements are for `g === "G84"` only, so the drill and the other cycles do not change. The test pins that the drill has no `M29`.
5. The option is a boolean post option in the group "Cycles & arcs". The title is "Rigid tap M29 before G84". The description is plain English. The Post dialog shows one more Fanuc row. The scroll gutter of #3388/#3392 holds it.
6. `crates/post/tests/fanuc_rigid_tap.rs` has four tests on a recorded CL stream (3 tap holes, then 1 drill) and a probe section at 0 rpm. They pin: no `M29` by default, `M29 S600` on the block immediately before each `G84`, the count of `M29`, the named refusal, and the default `false`. The test with the option off does not compare bytes. The byte identity rests on the reading in item 1 and on the goldens.
7. Heavy lanes. The PR body says "No heavy lanes run". The review of the head says that `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` ran 27 steps and passed. The red main of #3486 (three motion tests) is not related to this diff.

What a reading cannot judge (a control or a machine run is necessary):

- The order `S600 M3` at the section start, then `M29 S600` with the spindle on. The decision file cites B-64604EN-2 only for "M29 S before G84" and "rigid mode ends at G80". It does not say if this control needs `M5` before `M29`. Many controls accept `M29` with the spindle on, but the owner's 31i-A5 must show it.
- The spindle state after `G80` ends rigid mode. On some controls the spindle stays stopped. The post keeps `spindleOn` true. The next section writes `S M3` again only when the stream gives a new `PARAM SpindleSpeed` (lines 674 and 755).
- A `PARAM SpindleSpeed` in the middle of a tap section. Then `M29 S` writes the new speed, but the `S M3` block is not written again. The stream does not usually do this.
- That the feed of the stream is pitch x rpm. The post does not check it.
